action.description: Which read operation to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "find" pairs with find: {...}).

expandEventId.description: Optional event ID to expand with full content. Use this when you need the complete content of a specific event in the timeline (e.g., full email body, meeting transcript). The event content will be returned in requestedEvent. NOTE: for external_crm events specifically, use mail.fetch-full-event-content instead — this path has no formatter for that event type.

startDate.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime — only include timeline events that occurred ON or AFTER this date.

endDate.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime — only include timeline events that occurred ON or BEFORE this date.

eventTypes.description: Optional list of event types to include in the timeline. If omitted, all event types are included. Valid values: email, slack_message, meeting, external_crm.

write_to_file.description: When true, fetches ALL full event content (email bodies, meeting transcripts, etc.) and writes everything to a TASK_BUFFER doc. The result will contain path and access_instructions — use these to read or search the buffer. Use this when you need the actual content of emails or transcripts. Without write_to_file, only a brief timeline summary is returned.

showStageChanges.description: When true, injects stage change milestones from the deal history into the timeline. Use only when you need to understand when the deal moved between stages — for analysis, wiki extraction, or understanding the deal arc. Default: false.

includePlaybook.description: Whether to inline the full rendered playbook in `agentOperatingProcedure`. Default false: the playbook is often 40KB+, so it's omitted and `agentOperatingProcedure` instead carries a short directive naming the deal's playbook (aopId) and the exact tool call to read it in full when you actually need to decide behavior. `domainGuidance` is returned either way. Set true only when you specifically want the whole playbook inlined up front.

field.description: The field to filter on: a standard field (see the enum) OR a custom field as "wm_<fieldKey>" (the ids in <available_columns>) — custom fields match on their current value with eq/neq/like/ilike/in/notIn/isNull/isNotNull, or gt/gte/lt/lte on date-shaped values.

value.description: The value to compare against. Not needed for isNull/isNotNull operators. For ilike, use % as wildcard (e.g., "%corgi%" for contains).

filters.description: Filter conditions, ANDed together. Filter ANY field: standard columns (name, status, priority, dealValue, nextStepDate, lastContactedAt, aopName, primaryCompanyName, ownerId, …), computed booleans (crmSynced, hasFutureCalendar), or custom fields as "wm_<fieldKey>" (the ids in <available_columns>). e.g. [{"field":"status","operator":"in","value":["pilot_planned"]},{"field":"crmSynced","operator":"eq","value":true}]. For a name/company text search use an "ilike" filter (e.g. {"field":"primaryCompanyName","operator":"ilike","value":"%acme%"}). For the "ownerId" field pass the literal "self" to scope to the calling user (resolved server-side). SCOPE: results are ORG-WIDE by default — every conversation in the caller's organization, including other members'. When the user asks about THEIR OWN deals ("my pipeline", "deals I own"), you MUST add {"field":"ownerId","operator":"eq","value":"self"} or the answer will silently include other people's deals. Each result carries ownerName / isOwnedByCurrentUser.

date.description: Reference date as ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Today is 2026-10-30 - compute from this.

dateTo.description: Upper bound date for range operator as ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

eventType.description: Event type to count (email, email_inbound, email_outbound, meeting, etc.)

count.description: Filter by event count (e.g., conversations with more than 5 emails)

eventFilter.description: Optional event filter — filter by event types (include/exclude) or by event count (e.g. conversations with more than 5 emails via count).

orderBy.description: Optional sorting. Defaults to lastContactedAt desc.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default 20, max 50.

extraFields.description: [flexible_query mode] Additional fields to include in each result beyond the defaults. Standard fields (camelCase columns from crmConversations): "nextSteps", "statusOverview", "important", "lastEmailAt", "lastUpdatedAt", "updatedAt", "conversationScope" — returned as top-level keys on each result. Custom fields: pass "wm_<fieldKey>" (the ids shown in <available_columns>) to get their current values, returned under each result's `customFields` object keyed by fieldKey. Unknown standard field names are silently ignored; list-type custom fields are not returned inline (they accumulate per-event).

query.description: The search query (already embedding-optimized by main agent)

emailClassification.description: Filter by email classification (e.g. follow-up, initial-outreach, post-meeting, pre-meeting, reactivation, question, response, objection)

filters.description: Filters to apply to the search

searchType.description: Search method. "vector" = semantic similarity (default), for meaning. "fts" = exact keyword match (BM25), for a literal string — an order number, a URL, a name, or "Attachments" to find emails with attachments. Vectors blur exact tokens; use fts when the answer IS the string.

providerId.description: The CRM connection's providerId — get this from `config`'s `read-settings` action (sections: ["connections"]).

keyword.description: Search text — deal/opportunity name, company name, etc.

searchExternalCrmDeals.description: Operates on the user's connected EXTERNAL CRM (Salesforce/HubSpot/Attio/Copper) — NOT Cedar's own conversation records (that's `find`). If it's unclear whether the user means "search Cedar's deals" or "search our Salesforce/HubSpot", ask before calling either.

maxInline.description: Return inline only up to this many entries; above it the full timeline is written to the doc sink and a handle is returned. Default 200.

timeline.description: Read one time-ordered stream across events + both taxonomy planes for one or more deals, filtered by any combination of the cube. Masks: raw spine = kinds:["event"]; one field = fieldIds:["…"]; cross-deal = N conversationIds. Large results → the doc sink.

fieldId.description: The single field whose change/occurrence series to trace over time.

fieldEvolution.description: One field's change/occurrence series over time, grouped by deal (the "how did X evolve" curve).

at.description: Exactly one of stage | date | eventId — the point in time to resolve the value at.

valueAsOf.description: A versioned field's value + scores at a given instant (latest change ≤ the resolved cutoff).

describeField.description: Learn a field's filterable surface (plane, whether it carries strength/completeness, its vocab, and payload keys + observed values) before building a precise mask.

conversationId.description: The deal whose RAW verbatim event content to resolve.

rawContent.description: Resolve a deal's RAW verbatim events (full transcripts / email bodies / Slack) into a doc-sink buffer with greppable "=== STAGE: <stage> (evt_<id> @ <ISO>) [word_base: N] ===" section markers, then return only a handle + access instructions. Word offsets in the buffer are global; each marker's word_base + an atom's `position` gives the atom's global offset for a #words read. Read it via read-document (supports #lines/{a}-{b} and #words/{a}-{b} windowed reads) and search-documents (regex).

query.description: Semantic query (embedding-optimized). Ranks candidates by vector similarity.

filter.description: The SAME filter cube as `timeline`, applied to the semantic candidates. Only the cheap-to-combine dimensions filter natively (fieldId, conversationIds, stage, rep, sourceEventId, occurredAt range, strength/completeness range, current, payload membership); other dimensions post-filter via the pointer.

search.description: Semantic search over the extracted taxonomy atoms — discover relevant moments/deals. Hits point back (fieldValueId / conversationId / sourceEventId) so you can hop to `timeline` (shape) and raw-content (prove). Large sets → the doc sink.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.
